summary: Final backend-only retest of share-link _client_ip after the iteration_11 CF-range note. The code now skips at most one Cloudflare hop from the right (IPv4 and IPv6 _CF_NETS). Private, loopback, invalid, Google LB and TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS entries are still always skipped. I added TestCfRangeClient (4 tests) to test_share_ratelimit.py. It covers a WARP client at 104.28.33.7 with rotating left-side spoofs, varying CF egress, extra GFE hops, junk and private entries. It also covers a second WARP user behind the same egress (not locked out), IPv6 CF client and egress, and a chain with two CF entries where only one is skipped. Results: test_share_ratelimit.py 22/22 passed, including all earlier classes such as TestPublicMalformedXffBypass. test_share.py 16/16 passed. Backend was restarted before each run.
critical_code_review_comments: _client_ip logic is correct: walking from the right, the first CF entry is the egress and the next valid public entry is the real client, even when that client is in a CF range. Anything further left (set by the client) is never reached.

Accepted trade-off: requests that come direct to the Google LB without Cloudflare, with a client in a CF range, have that client IP skipped as the 'egress'. The per-token cap of 20 per 15 min still applies, so the risk is low.
_CF_NETS is hardcoded. Cloudflare ranges change rarely, but they need a manual refresh from cloudflare.com/ips when they do.
seed_data_creation: None. Each test class created a TEST_T1 project and deleted it by id in test_99_cleanup (all returned 200).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate-limit state is in memory, so restart the backend before each run. Run with -p no:xdist -o addopts="" so the class-ordered tests run in sequence. Test IPs must be public: doc ranges and 10/8 count as private and are skipped. LB 34.8.246.104 is trusted through TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS.
